evidence: mux.lisp:1157-1158 `((eq (fnn-mux-conn-phase conn) :proxy) (fnn-mux-proxy-expired loop conn))`, the only timer branch without a `due` test. fnn-mux-proxy-expired (mux.lisp:964-977) is an fnn-owner-serialized call. fnn-mux-proxy-readable also calls it before every read (981).
fix: Gate the call on the ACL2-provided hs-deadline being due, as the :handshake and :tls-queued branches already do with `(due (fnn-mux-conn-hs-deadline conn))`, and let ACL2 decide only at or after that point.
reviewer: mux.lisp:1157-1158 calls fnn-mux-proxy-expired for every :proxy conn on every timer pass with no due test, and that function is an fnn-owner-serialized ACL2 call (mux.lisp:964-977). fnn-mux-proxy-readable calls it again before every read (mux.lisp:981). Only trusted-proxy connections that have not finished their PROXY header are in :proxy, and those already hold admitted handshake slots, so K is bounded by the in-flight handshake limit. This is a performance and contention cost, not a correctness bug.
scenario: With K connections from a trusted proxy waiting for their PROXY header, every pass of that loop takes the global owner mutex K times. A pass runs at least 4 times a second and once per I/O event on any of the loop's connections. Under load, mutex holds scale as passes × K and contend with every served quantum, even though each deadline is seconds away.
title: Every loop pass makes an owner-mutex ACL2 call for every :proxy connection, whether or not its deadline is due
